title: Sundance Square
name: Sundance Square
metaTitle: Sundance Square 1031 Exchange Investors | Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Sundance Square investors trading restaurant, retail, and office space inside a district managed under a single operating structure.

sections.html: Sundance Square is a compact entertainment and retail district developed around restored early-1900s facades, most of it held and managed as a single cohesive district rather than sold parcel by parcel. That ownership structure changes what a 1031 exchanger is actually being asked to underwrite here compared with a standalone retail purchase elsewhere in the metro.

sections.heading: A District Managed as One Asset, Not a Collection of Separate Owners
sections.html: Much of Sundance Square operates under a management or operating agreement with the district's operating entity, meaning a purchaser's rights can run through that agreement rather than through a standalone fee-simple retail parcel. The exchange file should include a copy of any operating or management agreement in place, beyond the deed and lease, since the agreement can carry maintenance, signage, and use terms that a standard commercial lease review would miss entirely. That review should also cover the operating entity's rules on hours of operation, exterior signage placement, and any assessment or common-area charge tied to ownership within the district, since these obligations attach to the property regardless of who holds title.

sections.heading: Property Types Available to a Sundance Square Exchanger
sections.html:
A realistic shortlist inside the district includes:

  • restaurant and bar space with rooftop patio build-out inside a restored historic facade
  • office suites above ground-floor retail in one of the district's mixed-use buildings
  • retail storefronts fronting the pedestrian core near Bass Performance Hall
  • entertainment-use space tied to the district's festival street closures
  • a limited number of standalone parcels outside the core management structure

Turnover inside the district is slower than at a standalone retail center nearby, since most tenants who hold a Sundance Square location have already cleared the operating entity's approval process once and are reluctant to give up that position voluntarily.

sections.heading: Identification Strategy When the District's Management Agreement Is Part of the Deal
sections.html: An exchanger comparing one Sundance Square lease to another similar lease inside the district can typically rely on the three-property rule, since the replacement search stays narrow. An investor diversifying out of the district's management structure into standalone retail or a DST interest benefits from the 200% rule, which keeps a broader set of candidates available. An exchanger should also confirm whether the operating entity places any restriction on assigning a lease to a new tenant type, since that restriction can narrow the pool of buyers willing to take on a specific storefront.

sections.heading: Facade and Signage Restrictions Are a Documentation Item, Not a Footnote
sections.html: The district's restored historic facades typically carry design and signage standards set by the operating entity. Any planned renovation or improvement exchange should have the design review sign-off documented and attached to the exchange file before the identification notice is filed, since a restaurant build-out that assumes standard signage rights can stall mid-project. That review typically covers awning color, sign lettering size, and any rooftop equipment visibility from the pedestrian core, and skipping it is the most common reason a Sundance Square renovation timeline slips.

sections.heading: Coordinating the Qualified Intermediary Around a Management Agreement Assignment
sections.html: Assigning the underlying management or operating agreement to a buyer is a separate consent step from the standard deed transfer, and the operating entity's consent should be requested as soon as a replacement property is identified. Waiting until the closing table to raise that request has closed out more than one Sundance Square deal against the 180-day deadline. The exchange agreement should also specify who is responsible for any transfer or administrative fee the operating entity charges upon assignment, since that cost is sometimes overlooked until the final settlement statement.

faqs.q: Does buying a Sundance Square restaurant space mean I'm only buying a lease, not a fee-simple parcel?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Much of the district operates under a management or operating agreement with the district's operating entity, so the exchange file should include that agreement alongside the standard deed and lease documents.

faqs.q: Do I need design approval before renovating a Sundance Square storefront as part of an improvement exchange?
faqs.a: In most cases the restored facades carry design and signage standards set by the district, and a documented sign-off should be part of the exchange file before construction begins, since assuming standard signage rights can stall a renovation mid-project.

faqs.q: How many properties can I identify if I'm exiting one Sundance Square lease for a similar one?
faqs.a: Three is usually sufficient when the replacement search stays within similar retail or restaurant space in the district. A broader list under the 200% rule becomes useful when diversifying outside the district's management structure.

faqs.q: What happens if the operating entity doesn't consent to assigning the management agreement in time?
faqs.a: The closing can stall past the 180-day exchange period if consent is requested late. Requesting assignment consent as soon as a replacement property is identified, rather than waiting for the closing table, avoids that outcome.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Fort Worth guarantee the district's operating entity will approve my assignment?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates documentation and communication among the investor's advisors and the relevant parties. Approval of an assignment or design request rests with the district's operating entity, and tax qualification rests with the investor's CPA and qualified intermediary.

faqs.q: Does Sundance Square charge a transfer or administrative fee when a property changes hands?
faqs.a: Many properties inside the district do carry an assignment or administrative fee tied to the operating agreement, and that cost should be identified and allocated in the purchase contract before closing rather than discovered on the settlement statement.
